mechanism_narrative: Accelerating GDP growth, as measured by the year-over-year change in real GDP, signals a strengthening economy that will boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Yield curve inverts (10y-3m < 0) during the signal period, indicating a looming recession that will negate the positive earnings impulse.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in the unemployment rate below 4% signals a labor market so tight that wage inflation will soon accelerate, prompting the Fed to raise rates and depress equity valuations. This results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: CPI inflation remains below 2% over the next 6 months, indicating that wage pressures are not spilling over into consumer prices and the Fed remains on hold.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production growth decelerates sharply (3-month annualized change < 5%), it signals a supply chain disruption that will negatively impact corporate earnings and drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: ISM Manufacturing PMI rises above 60 during the signal period, indicating that the supply chain issues are transitory and not impacting overall industrial activity.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate rises above 4%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy that will slow economic growth and depress equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 10-year Treasury yield falls below 3% during the signal period, indicating that the market expects the Fed to reverse course and cut rates.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts growth accelerates (3-month annualized change > 20%) and the unemployment rate is below 5%, it signals a strong consumer demand environment that will boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Consumer confidence index falls below 90 during the signal period, indicating that the demand strength is not broadly based and may be fleeting.

mechanism_narrative: When payroll employment growth decelerates sharply (3-month annualized change < 1%) and the unemployment rate is rising, it signals a weakening labor market that will depress consumer spending and drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Initial jobless claims fall below 200,000 during the signal period, indicating that the labor market remains very tight despite the slowdown in payroll growth.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is above 3% and the CPI inflation rate is above 3%, it signals a high-inflation, high-rate environment that will depress equity valuations and drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The dollar index (DXY) rises above 100 during the signal period, indicating that the high inflation and rates are attracting foreign capital and supporting US asset prices.

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP growth is positive and accelerating (qoq change > 2%) and the federal funds rate is below 2%, it signals a Goldilocks environment of strong growth and easy monetary policy that will boost equity valuations and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The ISM Non-Manufacturing PMI falls below 50 during the signal period, indicating that the service sector is contracting and the growth acceleration is not broad-based.
